title: Connections on bundles, partitions of unity and embedding in Euclidean space
summary: Connections on vector bundles as generalised directional derivatives (a first look, taken up again in MAT-262); smooth partitions of unity and why second countability makes them exist; every finite-type bundle is pulled back from a Grassmannian; the easiest Whitney embedding theorem: a compact manifold embeds in some R^N.

objectives.description: Construct and use a smooth locally finite partition of unity, identifying the role of paracompactness and compactness.
Glue local metrics and connections, and verify their transformation and Leibniz properties.
Prove finite-type bundles are pullbacks of a tautological bundle and prove the compact-manifold embedding construction.

preparation.description: Read lecture 8: §8 connections as generalised directional derivatives, §9 partitions of unity, §10 Theorem 10.1 (the Grassmannian is universal) with proof.
Read lecture 9: Theorem 11.1 (Whitney embedding, easiest version) with proof.
Read Hitchin §6.2 (partitions of unity) and appendix §10.4 (partitions of unity on general manifolds) for the proof of existence.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A pointwise finite sum of smooth functions is automatically smooth.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Local finiteness supplies a neighbourhood with finitely many terms and justifies differentiating the sum; pointwise finiteness alone is insufficient.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An injective immersion is automatically an embedding.
commonMisconceptions.correction: One must also check the topology. Compact domain and Hausdorff target supply that step here.
